# Trigger

11 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `create_trigger`

*Additive.*

Creates a trigger actor (TriggerBox or TriggerSphere) at a specified location. These two shapes only -- for a brush-based ATriggerVolume use spawn_box_volume(volume_class="TriggerVolume") instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger_name` | string | yes | Name label for the trigger actor |
| `trigger_type` | string | no | Trigger class: "TriggerBox" (default) or "TriggerSphere". "TriggerVolume" is deliberately REJECTED here -- ATriggerVolume derives from AVolume/ABrush and needs a real UModel brush built for it, so spawning it through this path would hand you a success-shaped actor with no real collision; use spawn_box_volume(volume_class="TriggerVolume"), which builds that brush. |
| `location` | array | no | World [x, y, z] location to spawn the trigger (default 0,0,0) |

**Returns:** `{ trigger_name, trigger_type, actor_name, actor_path, success }`

## `get_actors_in_trigger`

*Read-only.*

List and count the actors that a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerVolume in the editor world (not PIE) currently reports as overlapping (AActor::GetOverlappingActors), without changing anything. Returns actor_count and actors [{actor_name, actor_class}], plus the trigger's own object name and class. The first actor whose object name or editor label matches is used; when it is not a trigger the call fails.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger_name` | string | yes | Object name or editor label of the trigger actor, such as the actor_name returned by create_trigger. |

**Returns:** `{ trigger_name, actor_name (the trigger's object name), actor_class (the trigger's class), actors: [{actor_name, actor_class}], actor_count }`

## `get_trigger_events`

*Read-only.*

Read the overlap-event configuration of an actor's primitive component: collision profile, whether overlap events are enabled at all, and which begin/end overlap handlers are actually bound. Read-only inverse of set_trigger_events -- it changes nothing, so it is the way to check a trigger is really armed before blaming the gameplay code.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the actor (must have a primitive/collision component). |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, component_name, collision_profile, overlap_events_enabled, begin_overlap_bound, end_overlap_bound, callback_bound }`

## `get_trigger_info`

*Read-only.*

Retrieves information about a trigger actor, including its type and bounding box.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the trigger actor to query |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, actor_class, is_trigger_box, is_trigger_sphere, bounds_origin, bounds_extent }`

## `get_volume_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a volume actor in the editor world without changing it: its class, whether it is a BlockingVolume, KillZVolume, PainCausingVolume or PostProcessVolume and, when it has a brush component, bounds_origin and bounds_extent as text plus has_brush. Fails if the actor is not an AVolume.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Object name of the volume actor in the editor world; its editor label is not matched. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, actor_class, is_blocking_volume, is_killz_volume, is_pain_causing_volume, is_post_process_volume, bounds_origin, bounds_extent, has_brush }`

## `remove_trigger`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Delete one shape trigger -- a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerCapsule -- from the editor world. The actor is found by its object name and its class is checked first: any other class, a TriggerVolume included, is refused and nothing is destroyed. The deletion records no undo step and does not save the level (save_level does). A name that matches no actor is a success with deleted=false, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). For a brush volume use remove_volume; to delete any actor with undo, delete_actor.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | The trigger's object name, not its editor label (e.g. TriggerBox_0, as get_actors_in_trigger reports it in actor_name); matched without case. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, actor_class, deleted (false when nothing was destroyed), already_existed (false when no actor had that name), note? }`

## `remove_volume`

*Destructive.*

Destroy a volume ACTOR in the world -- any AVolume subclass: BlockingVolume, PainCausingVolume, PostProcessVolume, TriggerVolume and the rest. Typed: it verifies the actor really is an AVolume before deleting, so pointing it at a non-volume actor is refused rather than obeyed (success false, deleted false, nothing destroyed). This is the counterpart of spawn_box_volume; for a TriggerBox, TriggerSphere or TriggerCapsule use remove_trigger instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the AVolume actor. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, actor_class, deleted, already_existed, note? }`

## `set_trigger_box_extent`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Resize a TriggerBox in the editor world by setting the unscaled half-extent of its box collision component and updating its overlaps; the level is marked dirty, not saved. Returns previous_extent, new_extent and changed. Each extent must be greater than 0.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Object name of the TriggerBox actor in the editor world; its editor label is not matched. |
| `extent_x` | number | yes | Half-extent along local X in cm, greater than 0; the box is twice as long. |
| `extent_y` | number | yes | Half-extent along local Y in cm, greater than 0. |
| `extent_z` | number | yes | Half-extent along local Z in cm, greater than 0. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, component_name, previous_extent: {x, y, z}, new_extent: {x, y, z}, changed }`

## `set_trigger_events`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Configure overlap-event generation on a trigger/volume's root primitive component: applies the built-in 'Trigger' collision profile (QueryOnly with overlap responses) and toggles SetGenerateOverlapEvents. Honesty note: this configures the component to FIRE overlap events, but binding an actual OnComponentBeginOverlap / OnActorBeginOverlap callback requires a Blueprint or native C++ class on the actor -- the cmd reports callback_bound=false to make that explicit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Trigger/volume actor name (required) |
| `generate_overlap_events` | boolean | no | Whether the component generates overlap events (default true) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, component_name, collision_profile, overlap_events_enabled, message, callback_bound, success }`

## `set_trigger_sphere_radius`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Resize a TriggerSphere in the editor world by setting the unscaled radius of its sphere collision component and updating its overlaps; the level is marked dirty, not saved. Returns previous_radius, new_radius and changed. The radius must be greater than 0.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Object name of the TriggerSphere actor in the editor world; its editor label is not matched. |
| `radius` | number | yes | New unscaled sphere radius in cm, greater than 0. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, component_name, previous_radius, new_radius, changed }`

## `spawn_box_volume`

*Additive.*

Spawn ANY AVolume-derived actor (default BlockingVolume) in the editor world AND build a real cube brush for it from a half-extent, so the volume actually encloses space: spawn_actor has no volume types, and a volume spawned without a brush has zero bounds -- 0 nav tiles, no overlap. It then normalizes the residual scale some actor factories stamp on placement (PCGVolume: 25,25,10) and RE-READS the brush bounds, so `success` means the volume matches the extent you asked for, not that the call returned. Typed siblings add one step each: spawn_pcg_volume assigns a graph, spawn_nav_modifier_volume an area class, spawn_level_streaming_volume binds a sub-level. Called with no class and no extent it gives a 200 cm BlockingVolume cube. One undo step; refused during PIE; the level is not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume_class` | string | no | Optional volume class (default "BlockingVolume"): short reflected name ('BlockingVolume', 'KillZVolume', 'PainCausingVolume', 'PostProcessVolume', 'TriggerVolume', 'NavMeshBoundsVolume', 'PhysicsVolume', 'PCGVolume', case-insensitive, with or without a leading 'A') or a full object path ('/Script/Engine.TriggerVolume'). Must be a concrete AVolume subclass; anything else is an error. |
| `location` | array | no | World [x, y, z] location to spawn the volume (default 0,0,0) |
| `extent` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] in unreal units, each component > 0; default [100, 100, 100] (a 200 cm cube). !!! THIS IS THE SEMI-AXIS (HALF-size), NOT the full edge length !!! extent=[500,500,200] builds a 1000 x 1000 x 400 cube and, with the scale normalized, gives world bounds of +/-500 / +/-200 around `location`. Check `bounds_extent_actual` against what you asked for. A value that is not an array is an error. |
| `actor_label` | string | no | Optional editor label for the spawned actor |
| `is_spatially_loaded` | boolean | no | Optional World Partition spatial-loading flag. Applied only when passed and the actor allows changing it (spatial_flag_applied); omitted, the actor keeps its class default. Reported RE-READ from the actor. |
| `normalize_scale` | boolean | no | Default TRUE: resets the actor scale to (1,1,1) after building the brush, so the world bounds equal the requested `extent`. It matters because some actor factories stamp a default scale during placement -- APCGVolume is spawned at (25, 25, 10) -- and since brush polys are authored in LOCAL space that scale MULTIPLIES your extent. Set it false only if you deliberately want the factory's scale; `spawn_scale` always reports what it was. Be aware that with normalize_scale=false and a factory scale != 1 the real bounds are NOT the requested extent, so `extent_matches_request` and therefore `success` come back FALSE -- that is the honest answer, not a bug, and `actor_scale` says why they differ. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, actor_path, actor_class, volume_class, world_bounds_extent: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, GetActorBounds -- kept for compatibility), bounds_extent_actual: [x,y,z] (RE-READ from the BRUSH component's world bounds; this is the volume itself, with no stray editor sprite in the box), bounds_origin_actual: [x,y,z], actor_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, after normalization), spawn_scale: [x,y,z] (RE-READ, as the actor factory left it), scale_normalized: bool (true only when a correction was actually needed), extent_matches_request: bool, bounds_tolerance_uu: number, has_brush_geometry, brush_built, is_spatially_loaded (RE-READ), spatial_flag_applied, success, requested: { volume_class, location, extent, actor_label, is_spatially_loaded, normalize_scale } }`
